text:
carmen: quick thread — ran a focused microbench comparing hot-fill (on-demand shard warmup) vs index-first streaming for safetensors sharded bundles. TL;DR: hot-fill reduces p95 for short prefixes, index-first has better steady-state throughput and simpler compatibility with existing manifests.

liam: can you drop the numbers?

carmen: sure. test: 1xA100, 384-token context, 8 concurrent requests for the same model. workload: varied prefix lengths (1, 8, 64 tokens). results: p50/p95 (ms)
```
prefix=1    hot-fill: 18 / 72    index-first: 24 / 110
prefix=8    hot-fill: 22 / 80    index-first: 26 / 115
prefix=64   hot-fill: 35 / 130   index-first: 32 / 95
```
notes: hot-fill takes advantage of eager shard mapping and partial mmap; index-first does fewer random opens once index is loaded, which explains 64-token advantage.

sasha: are these blobs with and without a bundled index? i.e., safetensors file with embedded compact index vs sidecar .index?

carmen: both cases tested. hot-fill especially helps when there's no sidecar index or index is large to parse. With a compact embedded index (first 64KB) index-first catches up.

ajay: two things: (1) compatibility risk — older safetensors readers expect a strict header size; adding an "index pointer" field in the header is backwards-incompatible unless we version it. (2) open() storm: hot-fill can cause a lot of short concurrent reads to different offsets — cost on cold storage.

sasha: proposal: add optional header extension namespace (like our model-bundle header) with a small fixed-length pointer area. e.g.
```
# header v2 suggestion (fixed 128B prefix)
magic: "safet0"
version: 2
bundle_flags: bitfield
index_offset: u64   # byte offset for compact index, 0 == none
index_len: u32
index_hash: sha256(hex)
reserved: ...
```
if index_offset==0, loader falls back to hot-fill. This is explicit and allows progressive rollout.

liam: i like explicit pointer. rollout plan? we can't change all existing stored checkpoints at once. We need a graceful decoder: header parser reads magic+version; if version==1, behave old way. If version==2 with index_offset nonzero, do index-first.

ajay: agree on parser. For storage cost and open storm mitigation: we should support a two-tier cache — in-memory small header cache keyed by bundle-id (0.5KB entry) and a local on-disk compact registry for bundles served from object storage. The loader first checks header cache, then registry, then remote. That reduces head-open QPS.

carmen: +1. Also observed that index parsing cost scales superlinearly with number of shards when index contains long varint keys. We should standardize compact index encoding (delta-encoded offsets) to reduce parse time.

sasha: another ops concern: atomicity during bundle replacement. If we write new bundle (v2 header + index) we must guarantee readers never see a half-written header pointing at invalid offsets. Options: write new bundle to temp name, then atomic rename; or keep a sidecar manifest with an atomic put.

ajay: metadata service already has put-atomic semantics for bundles in dedicated infra. For external S3 customers we should document recommended upload pattern (upload to tmp key then copy/rename). But we can also add a small "header checksum" area so loader verifies header+index_hash before trusting index_offset. If checksum fail => fallback to hot-fill.

carmen: good fail-safe: header includes index_hash and header_checksum. loader verifies; on mismatch, hot-fill. That gives graceful degradation.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary build with header-v2 parser bumped to staging at 2026-03-20T15:12Z :rocket:

liam: action items: (1) carmen -> draft RFC for header-v2 extension + rollout strategy (write patterns, checksum, parser). (2) sasha -> prototype parser + small encoder for compact index. (3) ajay -> sketch header cache + registry design with eviction policy. (4) liam -> run storage QPS experiments with temp file upload patterns and report delta.

carmen: estimating RFC will include compatibility table, microbench harness (we'll open a bench job), and a one-month canary. I'll put the RFC in docs/rfcs and ping on this thread when done.

sasha: one more note: let's avoid expanding header >256B to reduce first-byte-read overhead on remote stores. try to keep pointer area <=128B.

ajay: +1. also include cost estimate for extra HEAD/GET requests in the RFC.

carmen: thanks all. ping @liam @sasha for tests. :thumbsup:
